source_text: Καὶ τὰ χθὲς δὲ καὶ πρώην ἐν τῇ πόλει ὑμῶν γενόμενα ἐπὶ Οὐρβίκου, ὦ Ῥωμαῖοι, καὶ τὰ πανταχοῦ ὁμοίως ὑπὸ τῶν ἡγουμένων ἀλόγως πραττόμενα ἐξηνάγκασέ με ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ὁμοιοπαθῶν ὄντων καὶ ἀδελφῶν, κἂν ἀγνοῆτε καὶ μὴ θέλητε διὰ τὴν δόξαν τῶν νομιζομένων ἀξιωμάτων, τὴν τῶνδε τῶν λόγων σύνταξιν ποιήσασθαι. Πανταχοῦ γάρ, ὃς ἂν σωφρονίζηται ὑπὸ πατρὸς ἢ γείτονος ἢ τέκνου ἢ φίλου ἢ ἀδελφοῦ ἢ ἀνδρὸς ἢ γυναικὸς κατ᾿ ἔλλειψιν, (χωρὶς τῶν πεισθέντων τοὺς ἀδίκους καὶ ἀκολάστους ἐν αἰωνίῳ πυρὶ κολασθήσεσθαι, τοὺς δ᾿ ἐναρέτους καὶ ὁμοίως Χριστῷ βιώσαντας ἐν ἀπαθείᾳ συγγενήσεσθαι τῷ θεῷ, λέγομεν δὲ τῶν γενομένων Χριστιαῶν), διὰ τὸ δυσμετάθετον καὶ φιλήδονον καὶ δυσκίνητον πρὸς τὸ καλὸν ὁρμῆσαι, καὶ οἱ φαῦλοι δαίμονες, ἐχθραίνοντες ἡμῖν καὶ τοὺς τοιούτους δικαστὰς ἔχοντες ὑποχειρίους καὶ λατρεύοντας, ὡς οὖν ἄρχοντας δαιμονιῶντας, φονεύειν ἡμᾶς παρασκευάζουσιν. Ὅπως δὲ καὶ ἡ αἰτία τοῦ παντὸς γενομένου ἐπὶ Οὐρβίκου φανερὸ ὑμῖν γένηται, τὰ πεπραγμένα ἀπαγγελῶ.
orientation: Justin is opening his Second Apology, addressing the Romans about recent unjust actions against Christians under Urbicus and elsewhere.
pass_a_gloss: And the things that happened yesterday and the day before in your city under Urbicus, O Romans, and the things everywhere similarly done irrationally by the governors compelled me, on behalf of you, who are of like passions and brothers, even if you are ignorant and do not wish it because of the reputation of the supposed dignities, to make the composition of these words. For everywhere, whoever is being brought to self-control by father or neighbor or child or friend or brother or husband or wife according to deficiency, (apart from those who have been persuaded that the unjust and licentious will be punished in eternal fire, and that the virtuous and those who have lived in a manner like Christ will be united with God in freedom from passion, and we speak of those who have become Christians), because of the difficulty of change and love of pleasure and difficulty of movement toward the good to set out, and the wicked demons, hating us and having such judges as subjects and servants, as rulers who are demon-possessed, prepare to murder us. And so that the cause of the whole thing that happened under Urbicus may become clear to you, I will report the things that were done.

choices.english: who are of like passions and brothers
choices.why: Keeps the two participles as parallel descriptions of the Romans, preserving Justin's appeal to shared humanity and kinship.
rejected: who share our feelings and are our brothers
being of like passions and brethren

choices.why: Renders the odd phrase literally; it likely means 'by way of correction of a deficiency' or 'for lack (of self-control)', and the literal rendering preserves the ambiguity.

choices.english: will be united with God in freedom from passion
choices.why: Keeps the dative τῷ θεῷ as the object of union and renders ἀπαθείᾳ literally as 'freedom from passion', a technical Stoic term Justin uses.
rejected: will be joined to God in impassibility
will be with God without suffering

choices.why: Preserves the explanatory ὡς and the participle δαιμονιῶντας as a description of the judges, showing Justin's claim that the demons control them.
Keeps the infinitive φονεύειν as the purpose of the demons' preparation, preserving the active role of the demons.
rejected: arrange for us to be murdered

pass_b_english: Romans, what happened yesterday and the day before in your city under Urbicus, and what rulers everywhere are doing in the same way without reason, has compelled me to compose this address on your behalf. You share our nature and are our brothers, even if you do not know it and do not wish it because of the prestige of what you consider honors.

For everywhere, whenever a person is being brought to self-control by a father or neighbor or child or friend or brother or husband or wife because of that person's deficiency, the wicked demons hate us and prepare to murder us. They have such judges as their subjects and servants, as rulers who are demon-possessed. This happens because of the difficulty of change, the love of pleasure, and the difficulty of moving toward the good. I am speaking apart from those who have been persuaded that the unjust and licentious will be punished in eternal fire, while the virtuous and those who have lived like Christ will be united with God in freedom from passion. By those I mean the people who have become Christians.
So that the cause of everything that happened under Urbicus may become clear to you, I will report what was done.

last_rejected.why: ἔλλειψιν means 'lack/failure' of self-control, i.e., someone lapsing into vice; 'deficiency' misreads the sense.
last_rejected.ruling: κατ᾿ ἔλλειψιν means 'according to lack/deficiency'; 'deficiency' is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: difficulty of movement toward setting out for the good
last_rejected.why: δυσκίνητον means 'hard to set in motion/sluggish'; 'difficulty of movement toward setting out' is tautological and obscures the Greek.
last_rejected.fix: sluggishness in rushing toward the good
last_rejected.ruling: δυσκίνητον πρὸς τὸ καλὸν ὁρμῆσαι = 'hard to move toward rousing to the good'; awkward but meaning preserved.

last_rejected.why: The Greek is an exclamation/accusative of exclamation, not a relative clause: 'O demon-possessed rulers!' or 'as demon-possessed rulers!'
last_rejected.ruling: ὡς οὖν ἄρχοντας δαιμονιῶντας: 'as rulers who are demon-possessed' captures the sense adequately; not a major error.

last_rejected.why: παρασκευάζουσιν here means 'equip/instigate' (the judges), not 'prepare to' (the demons themselves murdering).
last_rejected.ruling: παρασκευάζουσιν can mean 'prepare'; 'prepare to murder us' preserves meaning without major loss.

problems.quote: Romans, what happened yesterday and the day before in your city under Urbicus
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if 'Romans' means emperors, officials, or citizens; First Apology addressed emperors.
problems.fix: Clarify Justin addresses Roman authorities or the emperor.

problems.why: Justin distinguishes fallen angels from their demon offspring, but the translation sometimes blurs this by using 'wicked angels' and 'wicked demons' interchangeably.
problems.fix: Consistently distinguish fallen angels from demons (their offspring).
